utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want to you think that I'm in a sadistic mood, Ms. Vidovic but there was no interpretation and probably you will have to repeat everything again. Is there a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I heard Madam Vidovic. One moment, please wait. I heard Madam Vidovic but I was not receiving any interpretation. And I am on channel 4. That's the first thing I check when I walk in. So I want to know for sure whether there is a problem with interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear on behalf of Mr. Naser Oric. With us this morning are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic and our CaseMap manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and my apologies to you, having had to repeat your -- so any preliminaries on your part? Yes, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Last Friday, you requested the Prosecution with a view to the forensic examination, our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We indeed had contract with the Defence team and it was with a view to the e-mail by the CaseMap manager of the 29th of September. In that e-mail there was a position expressed with regard to the number of documents and details of the number of documents, and also a position regarding the custody and the responsibility in that respect. Our position is, and after my contact with the Defence will remain, that this is not -- this e-mail from the CaseMap manager is not an official and formal request as requested by this Trial Chamber in an earlier stage, and still remaining are some questions like what sort of examination, what methods of examination, what is the time frame of the examination, and what is the location, together with - that's not the least of all - the safeguard procedures that should be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Madam Vidovic, I think we can cut this short. I had thought in the first place of getting you together round the table to speed this up with the least formality possible at this stage and then we would formalise everything ourselves. It seems this has not gone down well in the digestive system of the Prosecution so what I would suggest is that you formalise is by means of a proper motion and then we will deal with it accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think there might have been a misunderstanding somewhere along the line because, as I recall - I was just trying to find the part of the transcript - the last development was that we were not going to submit a motion until there was a registry protocol and Your Honour had indicated in order for the Registry to complete that protocol you needed from us just simply information, not any formal, official filing as to which documents we required and where they were being held and that was obviously our communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're 100 per cent right, Mr. Jones, there's no question about it but you know how things happen sometimes and the situation has now taken a little bit of a turning. So what I would suggest is we do it the other way around, that you formalise it by means of a proper motion, then we'll come back to you as soon as we have a feedback from the Registry, and you will have an opportunity to discuss it very briefly here, exchange views after the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine with us, just so you know we weren't -- by sending an e-mail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I thought as well. I mean, I was trying to have it as informal as possible in the first stages but we will have to formalise it now. So I trust you will -- and please do take into account what Mr. Wubben's concerns seems to be. In other words, some points that he has raised may become important because it's -- if they are going to be made to release original documents, which are not yet in the records of the case, and which are the property of the Prosecution, they may have an interest in making sure that any forensic examination does not contaminate those documents, does not ruin them or whatever. So we are speaking the same language here and you know exactly that -- what has been raised by Mr. Wubben is very valid. So please do take that into account and we will do the rest. But let's try to speed it up as much as we can because these tests, from experience I can tell you, we are talking of over three -- 30 documents and this takes time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it will be in the next day or two we'll file that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Now we have this -- any other preliminaries, by the way? Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It concerns our appeal that the protective measures for this witness be varied. Namely, I spoke with this witness for the first time upon his arrival in The Hague. Concerning this witness, the face distortion has already been awarded but conversing with him I realised there was some additional facts in question, namely his mother, who is 80 years old, lives in Glogova. She survived the Glogova massacre on the 9th of May of 1992. A brother of his lives there with his entire family as well, as well as his -- the brother's spouse and children. And he intended to testify on that matter, something that wasn't heard of before, something that wasn't mentioned, and there is also the spouse of his late brother who was killed, who was a local commander, and she is constantly exposed to threats and maltreatment by the Serbs as well as the child. When I asked him about their problems, he said that people knock on their doors in the middle of the night, that they sent messages in the sense of that they will be killed, and when I asked him to provide a document, I asked him if he reported there to the police, he said we didn't go to the police. My mother didn't do that, because they saw the people who participated and organised the events of the 9th of May when about 60 people were killed. Out of those people, two work with the Bratunac police. Those two, plus some other people, who are of key importance for the events in May, June and July of 1992, are the people that he is supposed to be testifying about, and they are either employed by the police or holding key positions in Bratunac. I just wanted to let you know that it would be in our best interests to hear his testimony in public because it clarifies the entire situation at the time, but should we do that, his entire family would be put in danger, his old mother as well as his late brother's spouse, their children, as well as his life would be put in danger in a far graver situation and that there is an objective risk as to their safety not only because he was supposed to testify about the circumstances of his -- the events involving his brother but also because of the people who have positions in Bratunac even nowadays with the police in Bratunac. That's why I wanted to ask for a pseudonym for this witness in addition of the face distortion that was granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who will respond to that on the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I requested that Ms. Patricia Sellers do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Sellers, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have -- do you have a reaction to this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, first of all we would object to adding on additional witness protection measures for this witness. We believe that this issue has been litigated now on three different occasions. The information that Madam Vidovic is saying that has just come to her basically appears to be a -- types of either threats that seem unrelated to his testifying at this Tribunal. This might be something that is happening because of merely who he is. The Prosecution has already said that, yes, if the relationship between this witness and a local commander whose name comes up repeatedly, if that is what poses the danger, that the fact of that relationship be kept in private session, but the fact that this person is known in the area, is the brother of a local commander, I do not understand how the anonymity will necessarily even achieve the purposes that the Defence counsel has set forward. He will have to speak about the events, he's going to speak about the relationship, he'll speak about persons, and in the local commander has been the subject of repeated testimony before Your Honours. I do not understand at this point that the witness protection that they are asking for would in any way protect him from acts that have already happened or in any way should alter the decisions that is Your Honour have reached on three different occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go in private session for a minute or so. Let me say something in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I was misunderstood by the Prosecutor. I just said that he was going to testify not only as to the role of the local commander but also as to the role of the Serbs who are currently highly positioned in Bratunac and in particular with the Bratunac police, and that this is our gravest concern as well as his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine we won't be long outside, maybe a couple of minutes. In the meantime I would suggest that Madam Registrar, you ask the usher to draw the curtains down and bring the witness in and, as soon as we start, we need to start in private session straight away. All right? Thank you. --- Break taken at 9.39 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, let me give you -- make a recommendation to both of you, Madam Vidovic and the witness. Please try -- since you speak the same language, please try to make a pause between question and answer, because otherwise Madam Vidovic knows exactly what I am -- what this is all about, because what you are saying is being translated, interpreted, to us in English and to others in French, and the interpreters have a very, very difficult job. And to be able to catch up with you, you need to speak slowly and allow this short interval of time between question and answer. Otherwise, I will start receiving messages from the interpreters' booths and I must say that they are always justified in their complaints. I know how difficult their job is. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to ask the usher to place a map in front of the witness. That is a map that we have used before. It was printed by the military geographic institute in 1967.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness, as is usual, to indicate some places on the map that he's going to be talking about. I hope that the witness has a pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you show the Trial Chamber where Bratunac is on the map? On the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bratunac is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please underline that place? Could you please mark Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to you point out Kravica for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kravica. And now could you please indicate your place of birth, the village where you were born, Glogova? Please, Witness, before the war, did Bratunac have a majority Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, was Kravica a purely Serb village or not, including all of its hamlets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Glogova, except for three Serb houses, was actually entirely Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims lived in Glogova, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate Konjevic Polje now for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the makeup of the population of Konjevic Polje before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslims lived in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now show the Trial Chamber the road from Bratunac to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the road passes through Glogova itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe to the Trial Chamber the size of Glogova, how long is it along the asphalt road and how wide is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Glogova spreads over 3 kilometres along the asphalt road and is five kilometres wide.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it stretches for three kilometres along the asphalt road, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is five kilometres wide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate on the map where the borders of Glogova Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are? And you can start from Kozjak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show Bandera? You've already underlined it. Can you point out the village of Halilovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please point out the village of Adzici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that Avdagina Njive is in the village of Adzici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since it is not indicated on the map, could you please write AV in the place where you think Avdagina Njive is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And actually -- but it doesn't matter. These places that you indicated, are all of these places part of the Glogova local commune, actually which were part of the Glogova local commune before the war or within the Glogova region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you have indicated just now, that's the area towards Konjevic Polje and Kravica, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate the hamlet of Mocila for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is Mocila a Muslim hamlet or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, was that also part of the Glogova local commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now point out to the Trial Chamber Donji Magasici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Donji Magasici? And now could you please tell the Trial Chamber, before the war, was Donji Magasici inhabited by Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donji Magasici was inhabited by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please show us the village of Drmna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the village of Drmna -- the village of Drmna, was it a Serb or a Muslim village before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now point out Pajici on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, was Pajici a Serb or a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pajici was a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now point out Hranca and Repovac for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of Hranca and Repovac before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hranca was populated both by Serbs and Muslims but over 50 per cent of the inhabitants were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Repovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repovac was about 50, 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Half Serbs, half Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please initial the corner of this map?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours I would like this map to be given an exhibit number. Witness, you can initial the map somewhere in the corner and also you can keep it in front of you because we will be using it throughout your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. D7 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D793, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One other thing, because the witness marked Ranca on the map and I know that there is another place called Hranca, no? And in the transcript all the way it's being shown as Hranca when I think we are talking of Ranca and not Hranca, is that correct? Or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me clarify. That place is called Hranca by the Muslims and the Serbs call it Ranca but it's actually the same place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That explains everything. All right. Yes. This map is being tendered and received and marked as Defence Exhibit D793 and it is being initialed by the witness. Yes, go ahead. And thank you for the clarification, Ms. Vidovic, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you grew up in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many inhabitants were there in Glogova before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Glogova had about 2.000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether or not the population of Glogova felt safe and secure before the war in 1992, when they were passing through Kravica or staying in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why? Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Kravica always hated the inhabitants of Glogova and they always created incidents on the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did they hate them? Did that have anything to do with ethnicity, faith, or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly it was a question of ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness, any incident that happened in September 1991? If it happened, and if you recall, could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the -- this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two young men were killed in the incident; one of them was Fora and the other one was Siptar. And Mevludin Sinanovic from Glogova was injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the incident happened and who were these young men who were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The incident happened in Kajici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is Kajici a part of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of those people who were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who were killed were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this event onwards, did Muslims spend any time in Kravica at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims did not spend any time in Kravica, especially not at night. They only passed along the road during the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember, in 1991, any reports about the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether at that time in your area you began seeing armed, uniformed people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to see those people in columns with armoured personnel carriers and civilian vehicles and they would take the road, Bratunac and Kravica, and the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether those were local Serbs or Serbs from some other areas, if you can remember? We are still discussing the pre-war period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can remember. Those people were from Kravica, Jezestica, and some other places.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the frequency of the movement of the vehicles was higher in 1992, in the first few months of 1992, on that road between Bratunac and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see then? What was moving on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used the road daily and there were people on the APCs, armed people, and when the APCs returned from Kravica, there were no people on top of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether, in April of 1992, on that road -- pardon me, before I ask that question, I wanted to ask you the following: Does that road pass close to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The road that goes through Glogova is about a hundred metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the second part of April of 1992, did you see some barricades on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in Repovac, Hranca and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As concerns the village of Jezestica, did you ever any knowledge as to what was happening there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a barricade there as well, in Kajici, and that was the road towards Jezestica. That's where the barricade was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Chamber what those barricades or road blocks looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were manned by the Serb police armed with automatic and semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us until when Muslims could use that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims used that road up until the 8th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That particular road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, during 1992, did you know of the existence and the activities of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a name of Miroslav Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Miroslav Deronjic was the SDS Bratunac president, as well as the Crisis Staff president for Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Deronjic? And if so, how?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Miroslav Deronjic. He was from Magasici and he used the Glogova road often. He would stop by and he often took the old road towards Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now move to private session for a brief period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear or see or learn of anything that happened on the 17th of April of 1992 in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see or hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Bratunac that day. I saw armed people and they were the Arkan's men, as well as some local Serbs from Kravica, Jezestica, Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any problems returning home to Glogova that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The very same police stopped me. I was driving a van. They stopped me in Repovac and again they searched the vehicle looking for weapons and they harassed me, provoked me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. At the end of April of 1992, do you remember whether the Muslims from Glogova received an invitation from the Serbs to attend a certain meeting? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you learn of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned it from Nezir Ibisevic who was the Glogova local commune president.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did Mr. Ibisevic tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told us he attended a meeting with Serbs and that he told him to pass on a message to the Glogova inhabitants, that they should turn over their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the sense of possession of any weapons, what did you have in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is located in a mountainous terrain. There were a number of hunters there, and the rifles that they had were hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the Muslim population concerning the request by -- made by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some people, the elderly, wanted to give away their weapons, but younger men didn't want to. So people were quite disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after the 17th of April in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now briefly move into private session again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So did they issue a particular ultimatum on that day to the people of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They set the deadline for the 27th of April. The ultimatum was for the handing over of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened afterwards on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people came to Glogova in front of the school. Some people who knew of the ultimatum had already brought their weapons and they handed them over. Some people didn't, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember who didn't hand over their weapons or, rather, people from what locations didn't do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People from Velika Glogova, which is a bit further away from the asphalt road as well as the people from Vladusici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't is hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for the remainder of the population of Glogova and the surrounding villages, did they hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. I remember that they were issued with receipts from the policemen, and the policemen took those weapons away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps we can now have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But before we break, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a geographical question. We have learned that Glogova is a place and a broad area of Glogova. Now when you talk about the school of Glogova, in which place is it located? If you take a look to the map, is the school in the area where we have stated Glogova and somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The school in Glogova is located in Glogova itself, next to the asphalt road, perhaps 30 metres away. And the mosque is there as well as the building of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So when you speak of Glogova, you are referring to the place which is stated in the map with -- indicated with Glogova; is that correct? If you look to the map, you see Glogova along the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The entire area that I marked is the local commune of Glogova, together with its hamlets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But if you speak of the school located in Glogova, it is located at the spot which is listed in the map as Glogova? There is a name Glogova in the map here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: When -- you have told us that Glogova has 2.000 inhabitants, are you now referring only to this place where we can read Glogova or when you speak of 2.000 inhabitants, does it also include the surrounding villages like Adzici and Halilovici and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. All together it has 2.000 people. Halilovici, Glagosici, Velika Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: How many inhabitants would have the place, the centre place of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, Glogova village itself, what was the number of inhabitants of that -- of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I marked on the map. This was the entire local commune of Glogova. It was called Glogova, except that we have the hamlets of Halilovici, Glagosici. Those are hamlets belonging to the local commune of Glogova. So for us this was all Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you mind, Judge Eser? But there was amongst in this commune itself which was called Glogova, there was also a village which was called Glogova. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what was the population of the village called Glogova before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe more than half of the population. It was a densely populated location, especially alongside the asphalt road, the three kilometres along the road. It was densely populated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the village itself, what was the population of the village called Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe around 1.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have a 30-minute break and we will continue immediately after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to have this part redacted? Let's prepare a redaction for this part. You're not objecting to this, I take it, Ms. Sellers, or Ms. Richardson? I don't know who is --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Your Honours. I have no objection except I would only ask if in fact that you're requiring that the Prosecution also refrain from using the name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I said I was not requiring it. I was just suggesting very specifically I cannot -- I know that I cannot ask you to refrain from doing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the only clarification I sought. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just suggested perhaps you could consider that option but it's up to you, obviously. I mean, I cannot stop you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have that redacted, if you prepare it for me, and let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have made that mistake myself several -- on several occasions so don't worry about it, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, we were discussing the events of May. Can you remember what took place in Glogova on the 9th of May of 1992? Early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain for the Trial Chamber briefly what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Early in the morning, on the 9th of May 1992, I was awakened by my mother. I was sleeping in my house. And she woke me up because she heard a lot of noise and that was the noise from the APCs and tanks and she told me, "Run away." I put on my clothes and I started towards Brdo. I found my brothers there, as well as some neighbours. Shortly after, the shooting began, and we fled in various directions. Together with my brothers, I left in the direction of some rocks where we hid.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see the events in Glogova from the place you were at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We couldn't see Glogova itself and what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see some people from that place that you were at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Witness. If you intend to mention the names of those people --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that those people were moving down towards the market in Glogova. Did you return to Glogova either that day or during the night, you personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We -- yes, we returned to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we returned, most of the village or rather most of the houses were on fire, and there was a foul smell. We headed down towards the fields to see what was happening with our families and when we approached our houses we saw dead people, our neighbours. And amongst them was Nurija Rizvanovic, Seco Ibisevic, his wife Zlatija, and Avid Junuzovic and we found our mother there as well. But she was just unconscious, but alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your mother survived the 9th of May 1992. Did you talk to her about what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. She saw the killing of Nurija Rizvanovic and she tried to run away and that's probably when she fainted. She was lying there for a few hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't need to mention any names now. Just tell us, what did your mother say? Where were the people who committed the killings from, the people who had killed the Muslims that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She saw some people and she knew some of them. They were from Kravica, Jezestica, and the surrounding settlements, and she knew some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Did you personally see anything that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, I did see something. We also went towards the shopping centre to see what was going on that day. On the road, we met Seco Delic, who had escaped from the execution. He was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we talked to Seco. He told us what happened that day at or near Dzafo's house where he escaped from, where the execution was taking place. He told us how they separated the men and took them to the river in groups and that's where they were executing them. That's where they killed them. On that day, about 60 people from Glogova were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything specific about Mustafa Ibisevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He told us about a really awful event that happened in Glogova that day. He told us that -- something about Ibisevic, Mustafa and his two sons. They captured them and brought them there for the execution. He hugged his two sons. It's very difficult for me to tell this story because I get very upset. He was asking the Serbs to kill him and to let his sons go. They didn't. They first killed one son and watched him suffer. Then they killed the other son, and then after that, they killed him as well. And when we found the dead, we found him embracing his two sons and lying near the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see -- you personally -- did you see the bodies of other Muslims who were killed that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the bodies of other Muslims who were killed that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already said it was about 60 bodies in an area about some 20 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now move into private session for a few moments, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this map -- this map is being received and marked as Defence Exhibit D797. Could you initial it or sign your name, please, on it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, were you able to move about the area near Cizmici in May and June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained to the Chamber already that the Muslims surrendered their weapons by the end of April 1992. I wanted to ask you the following: After that, did you obtain some weapons subsequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had some hunting rifles, the ones that were not handed over by some of the hunters. We also had some makeshift weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the hunters that didn't hand over their weapons, do you have in mind the villages you mentioned Velika Glogova and Vladusici, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you produced your own weapons. How, if you can explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some people, craftsmen, who knew how to do that and they would take some barrels and they produced guns. We called them Kuburas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the area you indicated just a while ago on the map, from Velika Glogova, across Vladusici Halilovici, Adzici, and Momcila, as well as Cizmici. In that area were there several groups who possessed such weapons as you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were those armed groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had four such groups in Velika Glogova -- can I make use of the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Velika Glogova, Vladusici, in the woods in between, as well as in. Cizmici, there was a group there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is referring to the map Exhibit number D797.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we could move briefly into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders that he be appointed as the group leader? Did you receive it from anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described somewhat these armed groups for us. Could you tell us whether they were always accompanied by many civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber how many people there were in the area of Velika Glogova? And I mean civilians who were unarmed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 1.000 people, 1.000 civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were those only people from Glogova or some others as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Not only from Glogova. Also from Hranca, Suha, Potcaus and other locations from the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they also Muslims who were expelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people you described being in Velika Glogova, did they have any sort of accommodation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no accommodation. They were in the woods and out in the open as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was there in Cizmici? Were there a lot of refugees there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The same was in Cizmici, a lot of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw the houses in Cizmici. Can you tell me in May, June, July, and August of 1992, how many people resided approximately in each of the houses in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that. In Cizmici, there were 60, 80, 90. In any case the houses were full of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain it to the Chamber, the houses in Eastern Bosnia, are they large or small?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were largely one-storey houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they large?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, rather large.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you members of the armed groups did actually have weapons or, rather, how many weapons did each of the groups have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each of the groups may have had about ten hunting rifles and some homemade rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained that you were together with the large number of refugees in Glogova. Were you together with the refugees or in front of them or behind them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in front of them. Further up ahead into the mountain or the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far ahead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About one kilometre ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you close to the Serb lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the 9th of May 1992, could the Muslim refugees live peacefully in whatever conditions they had? But could they live in peace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were attacks on a daily basis. There was shelling as well as infantry attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you remember what happened on the 1st and the 2nd of June 1992, if anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were attacked fiercely on the 1st and the 2nd, and the fighting was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they attack only those of you who were armed or did they attack the civilians as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They attacked all of us who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the atmosphere? What was the situation with the refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can imagine the situation. There was -- there were 1.000 people there, women, children, and there was panic. It is difficult to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there casualties on both sides, the Serb and on your side during that fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were casualties on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the attacks of the 1st and the 2nd of June, did you move about the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt the testimony of the witness, but perhaps we can find out exactly where this attack took place, unless the witness has said it and I may have not heard, but there is a description of the attack. Could we have a location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic? You can put the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will ask that question but I think it was mentioned already.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Witness, where were you attacked on those two Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Velika Glogova, Vladusici, and Adzici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I thought you did mention the first two. So now we want to add Adzici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the direction of those attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you from Velika Glogova, Vladusici --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I mean from what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Kravica, Jezestica, and the surrounding locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether you moved about the area that was included in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you come across some corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people you found, were they dressed in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They have -- they had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of such corpses did you find?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four or five. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find any weapons alongside those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were some automatic rifles, some semi-automatic rifles, and a pair of binoculars, military binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps a further clarification. The corpses you mentioned, were they Serb or Muslim corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people we found were Serbs, and we knew of our casualties.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. We will get to that too, but -- so we were talking about Serb corpses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the you shall tore put a Drina Corps Command document before the witness. This is the list of the wounded and killed in Glogova, the number is 04544250 and 04544252. Your Honours, we had a similar document before but this is a different one, from a different archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the first page of the document bearing number 04544250. Please take a look at the name under number 22. Miodrag Jokic from Opravdici, and number 26, Radomir Milosevic of Kravica. First and foremost, witness, I wanted to ask you this: Opravdici, is that a hamlet of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know either of the two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Milosevic, Radomir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether you saw his body on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there anything next to the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We found an automatic rifle, the pair of binoculars, and his documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the documents you found, on top of the fact that you knew, those people, were you able to establish where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniform did, for example, Rasim Milosevic wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the next page of the document. It says "the list of wounded in Glogova." The name under number 23, Milos Milanovic, then number 49, and the name there, Miladin Savic. Please take a look at the dates of wounding of those people, the 2nd of June 1992 in Glogova. My question is the following: Can you remember what was the main direction of the attack of the 2nd of June of 1992? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the area of Polom, Kravica, and Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to the map that is next to you, could you please show where Polom is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness retain this document with him because we will go back to it later, but I would kindly ask for an exhibit number for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, Madam Vidovic, will become Defence Exhibit D798.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the Serbs attacked from the area of Kravica on the 1st and 2nd of June 1992. Concerning there particular attack, do you remember anything that happened with a certain boy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the case very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain that for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Velika Glogova, that was the direction of their attack. I remember there was one wounded, Mevludin Hasanovic. He was a boy, still under age. He was wounded and he was in Abramovic's house. They passed by the house, and Drago, a.k.a. Takac, headed that column, and they burned him alive in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, don't mention the name of the person who told you that, but just explain to us who witnessed the event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother witnessed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. At the same time, did you hear of anything happening in Adzici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A person, a man, came from Adzici, and he said that 12 people were executed on that day, the elderly and women and men, and they were unable to flee or walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see their bodies later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We went there. We saw that they executed them and threw their bodies into the creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Serb attacks continue throughout June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How often were those -- did those attacks occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost daily. Always from artillery and then with the infantry came. First there would be shelling and then the infantry would move in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the direction of those attacks, when we talk about Velika Glogova and Vladusici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that already, from the direction of Polom.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, Witness. Perhaps I was imprecise. The artillery attacks against Velika Glogova and Vladusici, what was their direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attacks were from the direction of Brezak, Avdagina Njive, and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge as to the simultaneous shelling of Cizmici at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was Cizmici shelled from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Vresinje and Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, how come you know that the shelling was from those precise locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had some guys who passed by those lines, because they were simply not afraid. They wanted to go and see what was happening. And then they would pass on such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand properly that the people who went there saw that, they saw the deployment of the artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they saw the artillery there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said -- you mentioned the pair of binoculars a while ago. Did they have anything with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had that pair of binoculars as well as a hunting pair of binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The artillery shelling that you mention, in the course of July 1992, were there any casualties in Velika Glogova or Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We did have casualties.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these casualties civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly everybody, civilians and also there were some from amongst the groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now show the witness another document? This is Defence Exhibit D15. Titled,"Circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina before -- or the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the war."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at page 2, which has the number 00641760, and beneath -- below that I'm going to read a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps we can move to private session for a moment because another name is going to be mentioned. Could we move to closed -- a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, Velika Glogova and Vladusici, is that part of the area known as Glogova Planina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a village called Glogovac in the Bratunac municipality or is there a village called Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a village called Glogova I've never heard of a village called Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember in if in late July 1992, any military activities by Serb forces ensued in the area of Glogova, which was held by you, the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask the usher to show the witness a new document by the Bircani Brigade command. It's document number 04337365. It's a daily operations report to the corps commander. Witness, I'm going to read out a part of item 3 for you, which says, "Having finished the search and established the line, control was established on the Bratunac-Kravica road." Could you please tell me whether on the 27th of July 1992 it's true that some kind of sweep was carried out as it is reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was such an action but it was actually a Serb offensive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, how do you comment this part of the document that control was established on the Bratunac-Glogovac [as interpreted] road and our forces were deployed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, when the offensive began, they just passed on the Bratunac-Glogova-Kravica road. Now, however, they deployed more forces. They brought in reinforcements to the Glogova area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 27th of July 1992, did the Serb forces patrol this road and not only passed along it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they both patrolled and used this road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D799. Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could the witness please answer just one more question, Your Honours, and maybe we could go on a break now because, after that, I'm planning to use a longer document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that at the end of July or in early August 1992, there were fresh Serb attacks against you and your population in the Glogova area which you held? Is this correct or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we can go on our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, certainly, Madam Vidovic. This is always -- I try to keep it as a matter of convenience of the parties. So we'll go on break now, and it has to be 30 minutes because of the redaction that we did in the initial period. So 30 minutes starting from now. That means we will start at 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, my last question was whether or not, in late July and early August 1992, there were fresh attacks against you, and you confirmed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that. Now I would like you to look at document -- a document that I hope is still with you, which is entitled, "the list of those wounded and killed in Glogova." Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document, the list of those killed in Glogova, on page 1. If you can look at page 19 first, it says, "Rankovic Ilinka [phoen], father's name Radivoje, from Jezestica, killed on the 2nd of August 1992." Then you look at the next number, it says, Deronjic -- number 21, it says, Deronjic, Nebosa killed in -- on the 2nd of August 1992. And he comes from Magasici. I would like to ask you the following, this woman from Jezestica, is it unusual for you to have a woman in the ranks of the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is not unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber why it's not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I met Seco Delic earlier, as I mentioned that before, he talked about two women who were killing those people who excelled in this killing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say that he told you about two women. Were these women Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to you look at the next page, list of those killed in Glogova, and if you could look at the name under number 3, Vojo -- the list.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction those wounded in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the name under 3 is Vojo Abramovic [phoen] from Kravica. He was wounded on the 2nd of August 1992. Then if you look at number 9, Goran Bojic, from Kravica, date of wounding, the 2nd of August, 1992, also look at number 13 -- are you looking at the list of those wounded in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 13, Slavisa Eric from Kravica. Date of wounding, the 28th of July 1992. Please look at number 24, Sadiko Milanovic [phoen] from Kravica, date of wounding, 2nd of August 1992. Please look at numbers 29 to number 31, you have Nikolic, Slavko; Nikolic, Milan; Nikolic, Dusko; two of them are from Kajici and the third one is from Kravica. The first two on the list, wounded on the 28th of July 1992, and the third person was wounded on the 2nd of August 1992. Please look at the name Obackic, Stevo from Kravica. We talked about that earlier. Beneath that look at the number at Radovan Pavlovic from Kravica, injured on the -- wounded on the 2nd of August 1992, also in Glogova. Look at number 43, Drago Radovic from Bratunac, wounded on the 2nd of August 1992, and finally, if you can look at the names next to number 45 and 46, from Jezestica, both persons wounded in Glogova on the 2nd of August 1992. And just for a moment, if you can turn to the next page and look at the name next to number 57, Marko Tomic from Kravica, born on the 28th of July -- excuse me, actually wounded on the 28th of July 1992 in Glogova. Witness, I would like to ask you the following in relation to this. Earlier you looked at a document or an order on sweeping the terrain in Glogova dated the 27th of July 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this was an offensive actually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again, do you know where the attacks on the 2nd of August or on the 28th of July 1992 and the 2nd of August 1992 came from, which direction did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came from Kravica and Jezestica, from the broader area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These dates, the 28th of July and the 2nd of August, cited as the dates of wounding of these people in this document, are they actually the dates when there were fierce attacks from those directions on Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You can see from the lists where we were attacked from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you attacked -- you agreed that you were attacked at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this document, I would like to ask you the following: If someone were to claim that these people from these lists were wounded in Muslim ambushes and not in Serb attacks or the offensive, as you name it, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were attacking, they were attacking us in Glogova. These are no ambushes. We were in Glogovac -- in Glogova, and we were being attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whether you say Glogova, I assume that you are thinking of Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Velika Glogova and Vladusici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt but if the Defence would ask the witness -- is asking the witness about people from the list. This is a pretty extensive list and a few minutes ago, we heard Madam Vidovic read out a number of very specific names from the list. So perhaps we can have some clarification as to, is she asking the witness about all the individuals on the list, with respect to that last questions or about the names that she read out? Because I think absent some clarification, it's going to be very confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Your last question to the witness, was the following: Regarding this document -- now, Ms. Richardson, please follow me, "Regarding this document," this is Madam Vidovic's question, "I would like to ask you the following: If someone were to claim that these people from these lists were wounded in Muslim ambushes and not in Serb attacks or the offensive, as you name it, would that be correct?" Now, when she put the question I was taking that she was asking with regard to all the people mentioned in that list, but if that is not the case, then perhaps it's the case of clarifying it. I mean, I don't know what you had in mind but reading the transcript, to me it means all those people in that list. But if the witness may have misunderstood you, maybe, or that's not what you intended, then perhaps you can rephrase your question and the witness will answer it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I discussed the dates with the witness. I was talking about the 27th of July 1992 and the 2nd of August 1992. These were the dates, after the document that we looked at earlier and I think that I was completely clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, I would like to clearly ask you the following: If anyone were to claim that the people or that the Serbs that I -- whose names I read out to you from this list were wounded on the 27th of July and the 2nd of August 1992, in Muslim ambushes, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you both.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That has served to clear up this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the witness to look at a new document. Could the usher please distribute the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at this document? It's an order by Mile Jovanovic [phoen], detachment commander dated the 4th of August 1992 and it has number 0435380 -- 262, and I'm going to quote from item 1 of the document. It states, "On the 4th of August 1992, a sweep of the terrain will be carried out along the axis of Repovac, Mihailici [phoen] Slapasnica, Vitkovici, Polom, towards Kravica, Glogova, Malasici, with the objective of establishing a front line, Vresinje, Bozici, Lemesac, Ladja, Kaolin, Petokraka, Zuti Most." First of all I would like to ask you if you can indicate for the Trial Chamber on the map where Repovac, Mihalovici [phoen], Slapasnica, Vitkovici, and Polom are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please point that out? Repovac? Perhaps the other one was better, if you think that the other one was better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repovac, Mihaljevici [phoen], Slapasnica, Vitkovici, and Polom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked these places on Defence Exhibit D793.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you the following: Do you recall the events on the 4th of August 1992 in the part of Glogova that you held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the terrain searched in the Glogova section that you held on that day? Can you please describe to the Trial Chamber what happened on the 4th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this part where we were attacked by them. The Serb soldiers made a frontal attack, meaning that a soldier from soldier separated some ten metres and they are going forward and sweeping the terrain. On that day, we had to leave the places where we happened to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, they managed to push you back or cleanse you from that terrain. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber where you were cleansed from? Because you were in different places. Could you be very specific about the places? And you can use any map you like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were swept back from Velika Glogova, Vladusici and from these forests or these woods where these people were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Vidovic? Yes, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The witness has already answered the question but I would only ask Madam Vidovic not to lead too much and perhaps the witness could, in his own words, characterise whether they were pushed back and what was going on following the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Ms. Vidovic. Go ahead. Have you finished with this document or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have, Your Honour. Could we please give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document, consisting of two pages, and I'm going to read the ERN because it didn't register correctly in the transcript. ERN number is 04358262, consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, and it is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D800. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the Prosecutor's remark. Could you please explain for the Chamber what happened with the population of Velika Glogova, Vladusici, and the refugee settlements that were in the woods that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were attacked from the areas I mentioned and they moved in front alley and in a line. From one soldier to the next there was a space of about ten metres. They were sweeping the terrain and we were pushed back to the village of Cizmici, with all of the people that were there as well with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Chamber briefly what happened between the 4th of August 1992 and the 8th of August 1992, concerning Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Between the 4th and the 8th of August, the shelling occurred daily from Vresinje, Jezestica, Kravica, and Magasici. There was daily shelling as well as infantry attacks. They wanted to destroy us then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, please. How do you know that those attacks came from Vresinje, Jezestica, Kravica, and Magasici, that they came from those specific places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had some of our people who reconnoitered their lines and that then they would pass on the information as to what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To go back to the 8th of August 1992, perhaps a bit later, but before that, I wanted to ask you something else. Have you ever heard of the 16th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that brigade from the area of Srebrenica when you learned of its existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That brigade was not from the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
