utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you learn about that brigade, who were those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our people who were in Cizmici went to Konjevic Polje to get food, and on their way back, they told us that Nurif came and that he is in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you found out that anyone else came with Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He brought along some 400 well-armed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if anyone else came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A physician, a doctor, came by the name of Nedret Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you learn that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From those people who came, from Konjevic Polje to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please show the next document to the witness, D647. That is the list of conscripts that crossed over to the free territory on the 27th of July 1992, as the 16th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have that list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at page 12 in Bosnian and page 15 in the English version for the Chamber. That page belongs -- begins with the name Rasim Osmanovic. Please take a look at the bottom of the page, the fifth or the sixth name from the end, it says Nurif Rizvanovic, son of Nurija. Is that the person that you said brought that group of soldiers with him, the 16th Muslim Brigade, to the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you heard of this Nurif Rizvanovic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a neighbour of mine from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we leave this document with the witness, please, because we will come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, to go back to the events of the 8th of August 1992, early in the morning. Do you remember what took place on the 8th of August 1992, early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 8th of August 1992, as well as the few days before that, we were exposed to a strong, heavy artillery shelling on Cizmici and there were between 1.000 and 1500 inhabitants there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, was there any attack on some other villages, Muslim villages, in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shoes nary, Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Witness. Where did that attack come from? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cizmici was attacked from Vresinje and Jezestica and the other part was attacked from the part of Brezova Njiva and Jaglici were attacked Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. from Jezestica and Djermani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that this was so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said already, we had the people who had binoculars and they were observing the enemy lines and they knew exactly from which direction attacks came.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That morning, the 8th of August 1992, in Cizmici, did you suffer any casualties as a result of that attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were a lot of wounded and killed, both civilians and the people belonging to our groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why there were so many killed and wounded civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they were shelling the village of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were those people sleeping outside or were some of them inside as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of them slept out in the open because not all of them could fit in. Cizmici is a small village and they didn't fit inside the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the Muslim population concerning the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People decided either to be killed there or to drive those forces away, the forces shelling, and they decided to move forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember how many civilians were there in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said about one, one and a half thousand.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other way out at that moment, apart from attacking the attackers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was no other way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what followed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Registrar, Madam Registrar, you know exactly which part to -- just that, all right? Thank you. Yes, yes, but she knows, I mean in the meantime because the other one will remain, part of it remain. Let's continue, Ms. Vidovic, and we will take care of the redaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those 100 or 150 people that you mentioned who went towards Vresinje, were they all armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none of us were -- not all of us were armed. Perhaps one-third was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain for the Chamber why the people who went with you were largely unarmed but before that I wanted to ask you the following: The remainder of the group that went with you, did you consider them to be fighters or civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then perhaps you can tell me why did those people accompany you although they were unarmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went along because, should somebody get wounded or killed, they would pick up their weapon, whereas some other people would take the killed or the wounded and take them back to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 8th of August 1992, and on that day, did any of you who started towards Vresinje, were you wearing any sort of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no uniforms whatsoever. We were in civilian clothes, no uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you reach the Serb lines at Vresinje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We managed to push them back from Vresinje and we went further to their artillery positions, up to an oak wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please pause a moment and show the oak wood on the map, please. If it's not marked on the map, perhaps you can show us where it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you at least approximately point out the location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps around here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we for a moment move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, I would need the technicians to possibly focus that part a little bit better so that I can -- okay. The witness has indicated with an A, a spot --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the letter H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: H, okay. Thank you. Above the village of Blazijevici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that the witness is not clear whether the Hrastik is actually a name of a location or an oak wood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understood it to be that he was indicating the oak wood. That's how I understood your question to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we were actually discussing a location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your question was the following. Please pause a moment and show the oak wood on the map. Then if it's not marked on the map, perhaps you can show us where it is. And then he said it's not on the map and then question, "could you at least approximately point out the location." So all the way I was understanding that he was indicating where the oak wood was. If it's not, he can explain what H stands for and of course his explanation --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We were talking about a settlement called Hrastik although a wood, an oak wood, would bear the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you have the settlement of Hrastik in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I was misunderstood by the interpreters. Who headed your group once you reached Hrastik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked that we move into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are not in private session as yet, we had not yet moved in private session. So let's redact this part and move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened at Hrastik, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Hrastik or just below it, at the entrance, we came across a minefield. There were a lot of killed and wounded there, dozens actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you step on a mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone close to you step on a mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A good friend of mine did. His name was Mustafa Ibrahimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since he was a good friend of mine and I thought I could help, I picked him up and I carried him towards Cizmici, together with the help of others.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how the events progressed? Did you discuss this with your local commander or the group leader? Did you discuss the events that followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about it once they returned to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told us the following, that there was combat and that a reinforcement came from Kravica and that they could no longer stay there and they had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What composed that reinforcement from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an infantry reinforcement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Either on that day or any other day, did you meet with Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that same day, in Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present during a certain conversation between a -- between the local group leader and Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was, since we stayed in the same house; seven or eight of us were in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did Nurif Rizvanovic talk to? Perhaps just give us the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He spoke with Ejub.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- were you there during the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if Nurif came by himself or whether he brought some other people with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A large group came with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I could see, about 200.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were those people wearing, the people that came -- who came with Nurif?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have anything on their heads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Green berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any insignia on the berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a crescent, as well as a star and two badges that I couldn't recognise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So a white crescent and a star, is that something that can be seen on the many flags of Muslim countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up until 1995, apart from this particular event, did you ever see such insignia before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please show four photographs to the witness? Together with these photographs I wanted to submit a letter from Mr. Fahrudin Omerovic who is a photographer and he gave me those photographs upon my request and this is his letter. He made those photographs. I wanted to ask the witness to take a look at the pictures. I marked them on their back with numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Witness, could you please take a look at photograph number 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could put it on the ELMO. A bit down so that we can see the insignia on the beret.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise anyone on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I know the man on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the one with the beret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber who it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Refik Hasanovic of Mihajljevici [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you during the war see this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him then for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "Then," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 8th. That was the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How come he came to Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came together with the Nurif's group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the photograph number 2. Concerning the previous photograph and the man you recognised, was he introduced to you in any special way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in that house where we were spoke and he was one of the commanders, perhaps a company commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at photograph number 2 -- no, number 2. The one that is on the ELMO. Do you know either of the men shown here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The one to the right. That's Huso Rizvanovic, Nurif's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him as well on the 8th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was with the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at photograph number 3 now. Do you recognise anyone here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The one with the beret. His name is Almaz Demirovic from Kasan Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 8th of August 1992, did he also arrive at Cizmici together with Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at photograph number 4 now. Do you recognise anyone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The person on the left side, his name is Hasan Ibrahimovic of Kasan Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you see him on the 8th of August in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following: All of those people who came with Nurif Rizvanovic on that day, were they all in uniform and wearing the berets as we can see them shown here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They all wore uniforms such as ones you can see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please give this set of photographs an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So what is going to be marked as Defence Exhibit D801 consists of the following: Four photographs marked sequentially from 1 to 4 on the back, as stated by Madam Vidovic, and described - these four photos - in a letter purportedly signed by a certain Fahrudin Omerovic, dated 28th of September 2005, same document being also available or made available also in the English language. Together, the photos and the letter are, as stated, being tendered and received as Exhibit D801. It's time, Ms. Vidovic, if you want to finish here and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it would be good if I complete this topic. Perhaps I will need a couple of more minutes to pose additional two or three questions directly pertaining to the photographs and the list before the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, Your Honour, perhaps we could continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We can continue tomorrow because I have another sitting soon and it's going to last another three hours. How much longer do you think you require for the examination-in-chief, Ms. Vidovic? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps another two hours tomorrow, I guess. So after the first session and perhaps half of the second session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So please, Ms. Richardson, be prepared to start your cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of October 2005 at 9.00 a.m.
